description:
You are a hydrologist analyzing the Muncie, Indiana (White River) HEC-RAS model to characterize the shape of the simulated flood hydrograph. This is needed to develop regional synthetic unit hydrograph parameters.

The HEC-RAS unsteady simulation has already been run. Results are in the HDF5 plan file at:
  /home/ga/Documents/hec_ras_projects/Muncie/Muncie.p04.tmp.hdf

Your task:
1. Open the HDF5 file and explore its structure to find the unsteady flow time-series output for cross-sections. Also identify all River Station numbers.
2. Select three cross-sections: the most upstream (highest River Station number), the approximate midpoint, and the most downstream (lowest River Station number).
3. Extract the flow (Q in cfs) time series at each of these three cross-sections.
4. For each cross-section, compute these hydrograph shape parameters:
   - Q_base_cfs: Minimum flow during the simulation
   - Q_peak_cfs: Maximum flow during the simulation
   - T_rise_hr: Time (hours) from when flow first exceeds Q_base + 10% of (Q_peak - Q_base) to the time of Q_peak
   - T_rec_hr: Time (hours) from Q_peak to when flow last drops below Q_base + 10% of (Q_peak - Q_base)
   - R_ratio: T_rise / T_rec (rising-to-recession ratio)
   - W50_hr: Total duration (hours) where flow exceeds Q_base + 50% of (Q_peak - Q_base)
   - W75_hr: Total duration (hours) where flow exceeds Q_base + 75% of (Q_peak - Q_base)
   - P_coeff: Peakedness coefficient = Q_peak / Q_mean, where Q_mean is the average flow during the period when flow exceeds the 10% threshold
5. Save results to /home/ga/Documents/hec_ras_results/hydrograph_shape_params.csv with columns:
   River_Station, Q_base_cfs, Q_peak_cfs, T_rise_hr, T_rec_hr, R_ratio, W50_hr, W75_hr, P_coeff
   (exactly 3 data rows, one per cross-section)
6. Save a human-readable summary to /home/ga/Documents/hec_ras_results/hydrograph_shape_summary.txt containing:
   - The three River Station IDs
   - A formatted table of all parameters
   - For each station, classify the hydrograph as 'fast-rising' (R_ratio < 0.7), 'symmetric' (0.7 <= R_ratio <= 1.3), or 'slow-rising' (R_ratio > 1.3)

Note: Python 3 with h5py, numpy, and scipy is available. Use the time step interval from the HDF5 file metadata or infer it from the data structure. If the exact time step is unclear, assume regular spacing and compute durations accordingly.

IMPORTANT: Ensure both output directories exist (mkdir -p /home/ga/Documents/hec_ras_results if needed).
